title: Grow without losing control: offers, members and the AGM

say: Grow without losing control: big offers, members, and the AGM.
This is the video for module three of Cooperative and Group Enterprise Management.
A well-run group attracts bigger buyers, distributors and programmes, because it offers more capacity than one producer.

say: But large offers can come with long payment delays, exclusivity, penalties, or a partner who wants a say in how the group is run.

say: Principle 4 says any outside agreement must keep democratic control by the members. And inside, a fair member lifecycle and an honest AGM keep the group together.

say: Ask four questions before members vote. Cash: how much must the group spend before the first payment arrives? This is working capital, the money you need to keep producing while you wait to be paid.

panel.heading: Test every big offer
items: Cash: what must we spend before payment?
Capacity: can we deliver, with a 20 percent buffer?
Control: does any clause give away power?
Exit: can either side end it with notice?

say: Capacity: can we produce this quantity, to the standard, with a 20 percent time buffer?

say: Control: does any clause give the partner power over our members, officers, prices or bylaws?

say: Exit: can either side end it with reasonable notice?
And be cautious of buyers or grant agents who ask for a processing fee first. Verify them independently, and never pay fees to a personal account.

panel.rule: Never pay a fee to release an order or grant.

say: For example, a retailer offers Kemi's adire cooperative 300 pieces a month at 9,000 naira each, paid 60 days after delivery, with no sales to any other shop. Each piece costs 6,500 naira, and the group has 1,500,000 naira of working capital.
Monthly cost is 1,950,000 naira. By the first payment, the group would have funded 5,850,000 naira.
So the committee drafts a counter-offer: 150 pieces a month, a 30 percent deposit, the balance 30 days after delivery, and no exclusivity.
That needs at most 1,140,000 naira, keeps existing customers, and still earns 375,000 naira a month. Both versions go to a general meeting vote.
Most crises trace back to a weak point in the member lifecycle. Apply the same written admission criteria to every applicant, and read her the bylaws in her preferred language.

say: Training is a duty under Principle 5. A member who can read the accounts is far less likely to suspect the officers without reason.

say: For disputes, start with a private conversation, then mediation, then a committee hearing. Before any sanction, the member always has the right to be heard.

say: When a member leaves, she usually gets back her share capital, plus any declared refund not yet paid, minus what she owes.

card.title: What a leaving member is owed
card.note: No share of the reserve. Figures illustrative.

say: Ronke paid 25,000 naira in share capital, is owed an 18,400 naira refund, and still owes 12,000 naira for a machine part.

card.title: What a leaving member is owed
card.note: No share of the reserve. Figures illustrative.

say: So she receives 31,400 naira, with a signed statement, by transfer to her own account.
She does not take a share of the reserve. The bylaws make it indivisible, so it stays to protect the members who remain.

say: At the annual general meeting, members receive the accounts, approve the surplus allocation and elect officers. Kemi's group had a surplus of 2,250,000 naira. The patronage refund came to 750 naira per piece, so each member can check her own refund.

panel.heading: Three jobs at the annual meeting

cards.d: Sales, costs, surplus and an allocation that adds back exactly. Kemi's group: 750 naira per piece.
Two non-candidates count. Secret ballot when contested. One member, one vote.
The community fund is spent on a proposal members approve, not by the chairperson's choice.

say: For elections, choose two members who are not candidates to count, and use a secret ballot when a post is contested.

say: Under Principle 7, the community fund is spent only on a proposal the members vote for, such as training two young women as apprentices.

say: End the AGM by agreeing your single biggest governance gap, such as no two-signatory account or no written surplus rule.

say: To remember. Test every offer on cash, capacity, control and exit, and counter-offer when needed. Treat members fairly from admission to exit. And let the AGM, the members, decide.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Test offers on cash, capacity, control, exit
Counter-offer with deposits, no exclusivity
Let every member be heard before sanctions
Reserves stay; members decide at the AGM
